title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 30
paragraphs: Having said this and kept his word, Xerxes continued his march. Passing by a Phrygian city called Anaua and a lake from which salt is produced, he came to Colossae, a great city of Phrygia, where the river Lycus falls into a chasm in the earth and disappears from sight, and then, after about five stades, reappears above ground; this river too empties into the Maeander. Setting out from Colossae in the direction of the Phrygian-Lydian frontier, the army arrived at the city of Cydrara, where a pillar set up by Croesus bears an inscription declaring that this is the border.
